column1: # Prefixes the morphology strips (comh-, iar-, neamh-, ...): a word not in the word list is read
# as prefix + a listed word, reported as MOIRF ("formed from the root ..."). The build expands each
# row into rules of grammar/morph-ga.txt at its @PREFIXES marker (the late ones at @PREFIXES-LATE; those for a capital after the
# Each row follows the same CO17 rules, so they are written once (tools/build-data.mjs):
#   - the second part is lenited (10.2.12, 10.3.5: deargbhuile, beagmhaith) ...
#   - ... except d, t or s after d, n, t, l or s (10.2.12, 10.3.5: antráth, seansaighdiúir)
#   - s is lenited only before a vowel, l, n or r (sh-); other consonants are never lenited
#   - a hyphen between two vowels (2.1.7(a): mí-ádh, ró-olc)
#   - a hyphen between the same consonants (2.1.7(b): droch-chaint, gearr-rás, gnáth-thuarastal)
# A prefix starting with a vowel may also take h-. Columns, tab-separated:
#   pos      the parts of speech of the root it attaches to: AN, ANV or N
#   min      the fewest letters the root may have, so that a short word is not read as prefix +
#   flags    space-separated, the exceptions (- for none):
#     hyphen        always written with a hyphen (2.1.7(f): an-, dea-)
#     wrong:2       the unlenited (or wrongly lenited) form is reported as non-standard (an-dhuine)
#     same:none     no hyphen rule for the same consonant; the root's first letter is left to rules
#                   written by hand in morph-ga.txt (ath-, frith- before t; comh- before m and n)
#     exclude:XY    letters the generated rules leave to hand-written ones (comh-: mh, n -> có-)
#     other:[...]   the root may start only with these letters, unlenited (ain-), or a lenited
#                   b, c, f, g, m, p
#     vowel:both    before a vowel, with or without a hyphen (neamh-aistear, neamhaithne)
#     vowel:nohyphen2[:letters]  before a vowel without the hyphen is non-standard; the letters
#                   are the vowels this applies to (ró-: not i, as several Dinneen words have rói-)
#     late:plain    the rules for an unlenited root go at @PREFIXES-LATE, after the verb-ending
#                   standardisations, so that foluíonn is not read as fo + luíonn
